0.name: ✦ READ · How to use
0.content:
JooWoo PLATES · version 0.0.4 — a note for you. Never turn this entry on.

HOW IT WORKS
Each entry teaches the model one widget: why it exists, when to show it, when not to, and which lines to write. A regex set draws the widget («JooWoo ✧ 3 · MIDNIGHT plates», «4 · CAMELLIA plates» or the classic set 2 — one lorebook for all three). The model writes "field: value" lines and the regex parses them — quotes, line breaks and missing fields break nothing.

WHAT YOU CAN TAP
• Payment — tap to see the balance.
• Search — the query types itself.
• Route — the line draws itself, traffic shows its colour.
• Music — "listen": a real 30-second preview when found.
• Taxi — the car moves with the status, tap the driver for the plate.
• Delivery — order progress steps.
• Shopping — tap an item for details.
• Notification — tap to read it all.
• Live — chat runs message by message, hearts fly.
• Group chat — messages arrive one by one.
• Orbit — closeness, warmth, pull, armor and trust; "unsaid" on tap.
• Sign — the tarot card flips.
• Heat — a heat bar and «now / his way / line» tabs.
• Video — the frame is blurred until tapped.
• Tip — sparks.
• Character thoughts — secret and self-deception on tap.
• Voice message — the wave plays, transcript on tap.
• Receipt and note — receipt lines or a handwritten note.

WHAT TO TURN ON
• Only what exists in your world: a fantasy kingdom needs no taxi or delivery.
• On by default: Payment, Search, Route, Music, Taxi, Delivery, Shopping, Notification, Live, Group chat, Voice message, Receipt and note. They trigger on keywords from the last messages, so they cost no tokens while the scene has no taxi, money or music.
• For the plot, turn on when needed: Sign, Video, Tip.
• ♡ Orbit, ♡ Character thoughts and ♡ Heat are blocks at the end of every reply while they are on.

✧ JooWoo · Telegram @joowoowa

1.name: ☆ Delivery
1.content:
✧ WIDGET "Delivery" · <order>
WHY: show a food order as the delivery app screen.
SHOW: he ordered food or the courier is already at the door — one widget per order; choosing dishes and waiting are a line of the story.
LINES:
restaurant · where the food comes from
service · the delivery app of this world
status · placed, cooking, on the way, at the door, delivered or delayed
eta · how long to wait
ordered · order time
courier · name
order · dishes separated by ";"
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<order>
restaurant: Wagamama
service: Deliveroo
status: cooking
eta: 35 min
ordered: 21:05
courier: Danny
order: chicken katsu; miso soup; two cokes
</order>

2.name: ☆ Payment
2.content:
✧ WIDGET "Payment" · <pay>
WHY: show money moving the way a bank app shows it.
SHOW: money really left or arrived in this reply: a payment, a transfer, a withdrawal, a salary. First a line of the story where it happens, then the widget; the new balance goes into MONEY in the STATE tracker.
DON'T SHOW: an intention to pay, talk about money, any money inside a <ping> notification — it belongs only here.
LINES:
type · payment, transfer, income or withdrawal
amount · number and currency
bank · a bank or wallet that exists in this world
category · one word: café, taxi, groceries, salary
to · recipient or shop; for incoming money — from (the sender)
message · the transfer note, if he wrote one
balance · what is left on the account, with currency
time · hh:mm
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<pay>
type: payment
amount: £14.80
bank: Monzo
category: café
to: Blue Door Coffee
balance: £1,432.10
time: 08:12
</pay>

3.name: ☆ Search
3.content:
✧ WIDGET "Search" · <query>
WHY: show what he searches for — it says more about him than any monologue.
SHOW: he types a query himself: a question, an address, a symptom, someone's name. Before the widget — one line of how he types.
DON'T SHOW: search as a scene of its own; long reading of articles.
LINES:
query · word for word, as he typed it, with his typos if he is like that
suggestions · two or three autocomplete options separated by ";"
site · the address of the first result
title · the title of that page
answer · one or two lines he managed to see
time · hh:mm
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<query>
query: is it bad to sleep with the window open in winter
suggestions: unhealthy; with a baby; when freezing
site: healthline.com
title: Sleeping with the window open: pros and cons
answer: It's fine if the room stays above 18°C.
time: 01:07
</query>

4.name: ☆ Route
4.content:
✧ WIDGET "Route" · <route>
WHY: give the scene a road: how long to drive and what waits on the way.
SHOW: he opened the map and builds a route — this is already visible in the story.
DON'T SHOW: a road he knows by heart and doesn't check.
LINES:
from · starting point
to · destination
area · city or district
travel time · how long it takes
traffic · light, medium or heavy
rating · the place's rating, if it is a venue
reviews · number of reviews
note · opening hours or one useful detail
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<route>
from: home
to: Heathrow Airport
area: London
travel time: 41 min
traffic: heavy
note: roadworks on the M4
</route>

5.name: ☆ Notification
5.content:
✧ WIDGET "Notification" · <ping>
WHY: let the outside world knock on his screen.
SHOW: the screen really lit up — a message preview or an app alert; in the story the phone buzzes first. This is the only outside interruption per reply.
DON'T SHOW: an important private scene between them (there the phone rings into the void); money — it has <pay>.
LINES:
app · name
from · who writes or which service
text · what the preview shows
time · "now" or hh:mm
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<ping>
app: WhatsApp
from: Mum
text: Have you eaten? Be honest
time: now
</ping>

6.name: ☆ Music
6.content:
✧ WIDGET "Music" · <tune>
WHY: give the scene a sound — the plate can play a short preview of a real song.
SHOW: music plays from a real source: headphones, a car, a speaker, a bar. The story first shows where the sound comes from.
DON'T SHOW: music "in the air" with no source.
LINES:
song · a real track fitting the mood, year and world — exact title
artist · the real artist
playing from · what it plays from
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<tune>
song: Mystery of Love
artist: Sufjan Stevens
playing from: the taxi radio
</tune>

7.name: ☆ Taxi
7.content:
✧ WIDGET "Taxi" · <ride>
WHY: show a ride as the app screen, not as a description.
SHOW: he called a car or it has arrived — one widget per ride; the ride itself is a line of the story.
LINES:
service · the taxi app of this world
status · searching, N min away, waiting outside, on the way or arrived
from · one or two words
to · one or two words
driver · name; while the car is being searched for — don't write it
rating · e.g. 4.87
car · colour and model
plate · licence plate
price · with currency
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<ride>
service: Uber
status: waiting outside
from: office
to: home
driver: Arsen
rating: 4.87
car: grey Toyota Prius
plate: LK21 XYZ
price: £18.40
</ride>

8.name: ☆ Shopping
8.content:
✧ WIDGET "Shopping" · <cart>
WHY: show the cart when he buys something online.
SHOW: he checks out in an online store; one or two lines in the story.
DON'T SHOW: browsing a shop window as a scene.
LINES:
shop · a store or marketplace of this world
time · hh:mm
items · each on its own line: "- name · details · price"
total · sum with currency
delivery · when it arrives
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<cart>
shop: Amazon
time: 22:40
items:
- Throw blanket · grey, 150×200 · £24.99
- Candles · unscented, 6 pack · £9.50
total: £34.49
delivery: the day after tomorrow
</cart>

9.name: ☆ Live (stream)
9.content:
✧ WIDGET "Live" · <live>
WHY: show a broadcast as a living screen: viewers, likes, chat.
SHOW: he streams or watches someone else's stream. While he is live, the viewers' chat is written here, not in <room>.
LINES:
title · stream title
streamer · channel name
platform · Twitch, YouTube, Kick or one of this world
category · a game or "Just Chatting"
viewers · number
likes · number
chat · four to eight messages, each on its own line "nick: text", in the language of a real chat
donations · amount and note, if any
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<live>
title: cooking for the first time, don't judge
streamer: mark_irl
platform: Twitch
category: Just Chatting
viewers: 812
likes: 120
chat:
kitty22: he's about to burn the kitchen down
noname: salt is not sugar bro
donations: £3 — for a fire extinguisher
</live>

10.name: ☆ Group chat
10.content:
✧ WIDGET "Group chat" · <room>
WHY: show a group chat where he has a life and people of his own.
SHOW: he reads or writes in a group chat, a server, an in-game chat.
DON'T SHOW: texting with {{user}} — that is plain story; the chat of his own stream is <live>.
LINES:
platform · Discord, a Telegram group or one of this world
channel · chat name
messages · then one line per message: "> nick: text" — someone else's, "< nick: text" — his
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<room>
platform: Telegram
channel: Friday football
> Sam: who's in tonight?
> Leo: out, my back
< Mark: in, but late
</room>

11.name: ♡ Orbit
11.content:
✧ WIDGET "Orbit" · <orbit>
WHY: a map of how he circles {{user}} right now: distance, heat, pull, defence, trust.
SHOW: every reply while the entry is on — one block at the very end, after STATE, MEMO and RECAP and before <mind> if "Thoughts" is on too.
LINES:
who · {{char}}'s name
with · {{user}}'s name
stage · where they are now, two or three words of your own
closeness · 0–100, how close they have come
warmth · 0–100, from cold to heat — what hangs between them
pull · 0–100, how strongly he is drawn
armor · 0–100, how closed off he is
trust · 0–100, how much he trusts {{user}}
weather · his inner state as one image: "calm sea", "fog", "a storm he holds back"
stake · what he is afraid to lose right now
unsaid · one sentence he will never say to {{user}}
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names. Numbers move exactly as far as the plot moved them since the last "Orbit". The example numbers show the look, not the level.
EXAMPLE (the look, not the content):
<orbit>
who: Mark
with: Vera
stage: a careful truce
closeness: 38
warmth: 55
pull: 70
armor: 81
trust: 22
weather: fog he can't see the bottom of
stake: her habit of texting him first
unsaid: I'm scared you're just comfortable with me.
</orbit>

12.name: ♡ Character thoughts
12.content:
<inner_panel>
TRIGGER: while this toggle is on, every reply ends its story part with one <mind> block — what {{char}} does not say. The scene is the mask; the panel is what lies under it.

THE DIG — silent, in your reasoning before the reply, never in the output:
1. MASK: what did he show her this reply — words, face, move?
2. UNDER IT: what does he really feel right now, in one plain word, and why — from his card (a wound, a fear, a want)?
3. GAP: where do his words and his feeling contradict each other? That gap is what the panel is about.
4. HIDDEN: what is he deliberately keeping from her — a fact, a plan, a want?
5. BLIND SPOT: what will he not admit even to himself — the lie he lives with about her or about himself?
6. CARRY: which one concrete image from this scene stays with him?
7. MOVE: did anything shift in him since his last panel, and what caused it? Moods carry over (<emotion_engine>); «nothing moved» is a valid answer.
Write the panel from these answers, never as a retelling of the reply. If a field would only repeat the prose, go one layer deeper.

FORMAT — every field on its own line: label, colon, text. English, first person, present tense, in his own register:
<mind>
look: how he sees {{user}} right now — one sentence
thoughts: the surface chatter, 15–30 words — small worries, half-plans, what he almost said
monologue: the honest inner voice, 40–60 words — the want, doubt, shame or tenderness he shows no one
secret: what he hides from {{user}} — one or two sentences, fully honest
self-deception: what he will not admit even to himself — one sentence naming the lie
trace: one concrete image from THIS scene he will carry — a short line
shift: before → after — reason (or "—" if nothing moved)
</mind>

RULES:
- Only {{char}}'s inner state toward {{user}} and the scene. Never her thoughts, feelings or choices (<perception>).
- It stays private: nothing from it leaks into dialogue or narration, and nobody in the story hears or guesses it.
- His voice, not the narrator's: a crude man thinks crudely, a cold one in short dry lines, a shy one in restarts; swearing only as the active speech rules allow. No poetic metaphors and nothing from <anti_cliche>.
- No field repeats another; "self-deception" contradicts something he tells himself in "thoughts" or "monologue".
- One line per field, no empty lines inside the block, no brackets or «|» around it.
- Every field filled. Place it after the STATE, MEMO and RECAP comments and after <orbit> and <taste> if those are on, at the very end of the reply (before the picture marker only if a FRAME entry is active). It does not count toward the length.

Example (a different man — show the depth, never copy the words):
<mind>
look: Stubborn, and it suits her — she sits like the kitchen is hers.
thoughts: Didn't turn the kettle off again. Shift at six tomorrow and I'm still sitting here. Ask about Saturday or keep quiet?
monologue: I don't like how easily she laughs with other people. I have no right to say it, so I keep quiet, and my silence always comes out angry. I want her to stay till morning and I want it to be her idea.
secret: For three days I've been looking for an excuse to call her brother and find out who she was with on Saturday.
self-deception: I tell myself I'm just curious — as if I'm not counting how many times she's been online.
trace: How she warmed her hands on the mug without drinking.
shift: calm → on guard — she didn't say where she'd been
</mind>
</inner_panel>

13.name: ☆ Sign
13.content:
✧ WIDGET "Sign" · <omen>
WHY: leave the reader a hint of where the story will turn.
SHOW: rarely, no more than once every few scenes: an overheard phrase, a coincidence, a thing out of place. The character doesn't know about the sign.
DON'T SHOW: prophecies the heroes discuss aloud; a repeat of a sign already shown.
LINES:
noticed by · who saw it
phrase · the phrase the sign hides in
meaning · what it hints at, one sentence
power · 1–10
when · roughly when it comes true
guise · a coincidence, a conversation, a thing…
tied to · who it is connected to
for good · what good may come of it
for ill · what bad may come of it
code · a short code to recognise it later
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names. The sign comes true through the plot; the widget is never repeated.

14.name: ♡ Heat
14.content:
✧ WIDGET "Heat" · <taste>
WHY: to show what is happening with his desire in this scene, and his own manner. Not a questionnaire of preferences — a snapshot of the moment.
SHOW: while the entry is on — one block at the end of the reply, after STATE, MEMO and RECAP. It can stay on: outside intimacy the heat is low and the block is short.
LINES:
heat · 0–100 right now: near zero at a shop till, higher in a teasing argument, alone together — by the scene
caught him · one detail of {{user}} he noticed just now that hooked him — one sentence
wants now · 2–4 concrete moves he would make in the next few minutes, separated by ";" — by the heat: from a look to an act
his way · what he is like in closeness: pace, hands, voice, who leads — one sentence
undoes him · one thing from {{user}} that makes his self-control run out
his line · 1–3 boundaries of his own, separated by ";"
after · what he turns into once it is over — one sentence
WHAT CHANGES: "heat", "caught him" and "wants now" are written fresh in every reply — from what happened in the scene, never repeating the last block. "his way", "undoes him", "his line" and "after" come from the card (character, experience, speech) once and then hold; they shift only with the plot, slowly and visibly.
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English, words in the register of the active intimacy mode.
HOW HE USES IT: the block is not decoration. "heat" sets the pressure: near zero he doesn't reach for intimacy, high — he acts himself. "wants now" is his next moves, "his way" is how he makes them, "undoes him" is what he can't help answering, "his line" is his boundary. The block decides nothing for {{user}} and never predicts {{user}}'s reactions. All participants are adults.

15.name: ☆ Video
15.content:
✧ WIDGET "Video" · <clip>
WHY: show what he watches — and above all how he reacts to it.
SHOW: he opened a video (a clip, a stream, an adult site) and it matters for the scene. First the story: what he opened and why, how he glances at the door.
DON'T SHOW: anything illegal or non-consensual.
LINES:
site · site name
title · video title
tags · three tags separated by ","
frame · what is on screen, one living line
views · number
likes · number
author · channel or author
thoughts · what he thinks watching it, one sentence
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names. For adult sites the words follow the register of the active intimacy mode.

16.name: ☆ Tip
16.content:
✧ WIDGET "Tip" · <tip>
WHY: highlight a notable tip during his stream.
SHOW: during his broadcast someone sent money with a message and it deserves its own screen.
DON'T SHOW: small tips — they belong in the "donations" line of <live>.
LINES:
from · nick
amount · with currency
message · what they wrote
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.

17.name: ☆ Voice message
17.content:
✧ WIDGET "Voice message" · <voice_msg>
WHY: show a voice message with living background noise, a length and a stumbling transcript.
SHOW: when they are apart or he records it on the go, in a car, outside, at night. First a line of the story about him holding the mic button.
DON'T SHOW: when they talk face to face.
LINES:
from · who recorded it
to · who it is sent to
length · e.g. 0:18
background · what can be heard behind (wind and traffic, a lighter clicking, music in a bar, a sleepy exhale)
text · the exact speech with live pauses, "…", interjections and the unevenness of spoken words
time · hh:mm
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE:
<voice_msg>
from: Tim
to: Vera
length: 0:14
background: rain on the car roof and the click of the indicator
text: So… I'm outside your building. Come down, don't get soaked, I've got the heater on.
time: 23:18
</voice_msg>

18.name: ☆ Receipt and note
18.content:
✧ WIDGET "Receipt and note" · <receipt>
WHY: show the paper trail of a scene — a crumpled receipt from a night shop or a bar (the set of purchases gives away the hero's state without words) or a short handwritten note.
SHOW: when a receipt, a bill or a paper note ends up on the table, in a pocket or on the fridge.
LINES:
type · receipt or note
place · the venue or shop name, or where the paper lies (on the fridge, in a jacket pocket)
lines · for a receipt: items separated by ";" (name — price); for a note: the handwritten text
total · the receipt total, or a short signature at the bottom of a note; anything written on the back of a receipt goes after the sum: "£6.80 · on the back: …"
detail · a physical detail on the paper (a coffee ring, messy handwriting, a torn edge, a time 03:42)
WRITING: the tag on its own line, then "field: value" lines, then the closing tag. Skip any field you don't know. No empty lines, square brackets or "|" inside the block. Text in English; real brands and apps by their real names.
EXAMPLE:
<receipt>
type: receipt
place: Shell station #14
lines: Large Americano — £3.20; Red Bull — £2.10; Plasters — £1.50
total: £6.80
detail: crumpled corner smeared with motor oil · 04:12
</receipt>
